historical_record.description: Shaff's furniture store was rebuilt as a three-storey reinforced-concrete building on the foundation and side walls of its one-storey predecessor, with the showroom and a mezzanine at the front and a furniture-repair shop at the back on Osage Alley.

The Mission Cultural Center opened in the old Shaff's building, which the City had bought for $400,000 after a campaign by the neighbourhood's artists for a Latino arts centre of their own; more than two thousand people came to the opening, a Mass said by the Nicaraguan poet and priest Ernesto Cardenal, who baptised children on the spot.
Galería Museo, the centre's gallery, opened with the Sixty-three Show of sixty-three works.

Carlos Loarca, with Manuel Villamor and Betsie Miller-Kusz, painted Spirit of the Arts, a 3,700-square-foot mural across the Mission Street front showing the work going on inside; its making was filmed as the documentary Anatomy of a Mural, and Loarca and Miller-Kusz restored it in 2017.

A renovation designed by Rosekrans and Droder, Inc., finished in January 1987, replaced the original storefront, built a theatre with a stage and dressing rooms, filled in the mezzanine for gallery space and made seismic repairs.
The neon marquee reading Mission Cultural Center replaced the wood and plaster canopy over the entrance.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its place in the Latino arts and cultural movement in San Francisco.
